BOULDY · TEAM BRAINSTORM · 24 OCTOBER 2026

See the app.
Follow the journey.
Decide what comes next.

A screen-by-screen guide to the current local app, its core features, and the planned community experience.

How to read this guide
Screenshots are real renders of the current frontend using labelled sample data, not real climber accounts. Current UI means implemented locally; it does not certify the deployed app or backend. Planned placeholder pages are shown honestly. Their future flows are proposals for discussion.

Getting started · 01Current UI

Welcome

Introduce Bouldy and give a new or returning climber a clear way in.

What happens here

  • Open Log in
  • Open Sign up

Flow

Returning climber
Welcome→Log in→Home
New climber
Welcome→Sign up→Home

Keep in mind

Signing in is required to open the journal. A successful sign-up also signs the user in.

Discuss with the team

Does this explain why a climber should use Bouldy?

Screen: /welcome

Back to contents ↑
Getting started · 02Current UI

Log in

Return to your own climbing journal.

What happens here

  • Enter email and password
  • Submit or switch to Sign up

Flow

Success
Enter details→Log in→Home
Failure
Submit→Read error→Correct and retry

Keep in mind

There is no password-reset or OTP screen in this frontend. An error keeps the user on Log in.

Discuss with the team

What account-recovery journey must we add before a wider release?

Screen: /login

Back to contents ↑
Getting started · 03Current UI

Create an account

Create a climbing identity and begin a personal journal.

What happens here

  • Choose a username
  • Enter email and password
  • Optionally add current grade

Flow

Success
Enter details→Create account→Home
Failure
Submit→Read error→Correct and retry

Keep in mind

Current grade is optional free text. The current flow does not ask for a preferred gym.

Discuss with the team

Should onboarding explain grades, privacy or gym selection?

Screen: /signup

Back to contents ↑
Home · 04Current UI

Home

See a personal climbing snapshot and choose the next action.

What happens here

  • Review sends, flashes and gyms
  • Open a recent session
  • Start another session through Gyms

Flow

Go climbing
Home→Choose a gym→Start session
Look back
Home→Recent session→Session review

Keep in mind

These are journal summaries. Missing history must not be shown as a trustworthy zero.

Discuss with the team

What is the single most useful thing to see when opening Bouldy?

Screen: /

Gyms and routes · 05Current UI

Choose a gym

Find a wall and start a visit.

What happens here

  • Open a gym
  • Start a session from a gym row
  • Open Add gym

Flow

Browse first
Gyms→Gym detail→Start session
Quick start
Gyms→Start session→Live session

Keep in mind

Gyms and routes are shared records; their permission model still needs team agreement.

Discuss with the team

How should users find the right gym as this list grows?

Screen: /gyms

Gyms and routes · 06Current UI

Add a gym

Add a missing gym without leaving the list.

What happens here

  • Enter gym name and location
  • Save or close the bottom sheet

Flow

Save
Gyms→Add gym sheet→Save→Gym list
Error
Save→Inline error→Correct and retry

Keep in mind

This is a short task in a bottom sheet. Duplicate-gym prevention and who may create records need decisions.

Discuss with the team

Can any climber add a gym, or should submissions be reviewed?

Screen: /gyms?sheet=add-gym

Gyms and routes · 07Current UI

Gym and route browser

Recognise routes on the wall and start climbing.

What happens here

  • Search by route details
  • Browse grade groups
  • Filter colour or wall
  • Add or edit a route
  • Start a session

Flow

Climb
Gym detail→Start a session→Live route log
Maintain routes
Choose route→Edit route→Save→Gym detail

Keep in mind

Only active routes appear for new climbing. The gym leaderboard link opens a planned page.

Discuss with the team

Which route details do climbers need to identify a line reliably?

Gyms and routes · 08Current UI

Find the right route

Reduce a busy wall to a manageable set of routes.

What happens here

  • Type a search
  • Pick a grade
  • Open Filters
  • Filter by available colour, wall, status or gym

Flow

Narrow the list
Route list→Search / grade→Filters sheet→Matching routes
Reset
Filtered list→Clear filters→Full list

Keep in mind

Available filters depend on the screen and data. URL/session memory keeps the browsing context after logging.

Discuss with the team

Are grade, colour and wall enough, or do we need route numbers or photos?

Screen: Gym, session and Climbs route browsers

Gyms and routes · 09Current UI

Add a route at a gym

Create the shared route record that future sessions will use.

What happens here

  • Enter gym grade
  • Choose hold colour and styles
  • Add route name, wall and setter
  • Save using the sticky action

Flow

Save
Gym detail→Add route page→Save→Gym route list
Error
Save→Form error→Correct and retry

Keep in mind

This is a full-screen form. Competition classification is labelled coming soon; it is not a working switch.

Discuss with the team

Which fields are essential, and who should be allowed to create routes?

Back to contents ↑
Gyms and routes · 10Current UI

Edit a route

Correct a shared active route without crowding the list.

What happens here

  • Review existing route details
  • Change grade, colour, wall, styles, name or setter
  • Save or go back
  • Open planned Beta page

Flow

Save
Gym route row→Edit page→Save→Gym detail
Back
Edit page→Back→Gym detail

Keep in mind

The editor accepts active routes belonging to this gym. Retired-route history remains readable. Closing the form does not save edits.

Discuss with the team

Who can edit shared information, and how should incorrect edits be handled?

Screen: /gyms/[id]/routes/[routeId]/edit

Back to contents ↑
Climbing session · 11Current UI

Add a route while climbing

Record a missing route and return to the active visit.

What happens here

  • Open Add route in a live session
  • Complete the shared route form
  • Save and return to the same session

Flow

Save
Live session→Add route page→Save→Same session

Keep in mind

The route belongs to the gym, not only this session. A completed session cannot use this add-route journey.

Discuss with the team

Should the new route be ready for an immediate first log?

Screen: /sessions/[id]/routes/new

Session journal

Review visits over time and resume the latest climbing context.

What happens here

  • Review the featured latest session
  • Open a dated session
  • Show earlier months
  • Switch to Climbs

Flow

Review
Sessions→Choose a visit→Session detail
Change view
Sessions→Climbs switch→Climbs collection

Keep in mind

Sessions are grouped by month with progressive reveal. /history redirects here.

Discuss with the team

What helps someone understand whether their climbing is improving?

Screen: /sessions

Back to contents ↑
Climbing session · 13Current UI

Live session

Log climbing quickly between tries.

What happens here

  • Use +1 on a route row
  • Open a route action sheet
  • Browse Today and grade groups
  • Add a missing route
  • End the session

Flow

Try a route
Find route→+1 try→Today count updates→Try again
Finish a route
Open route sheet→Sent / eligible Flash→Completed route

Keep in mind

Today and earlier visits stay separate. Routes already tried are projects or repeats; a new visit does not reset lifetime flash eligibility.

Discuss with the team

Can this be used with one hand between climbs?

Screen: /sessions/[id] (live)

Back to contents ↑
Climbing session · 14Current UI

Route actions and continuing projects

See previous effort and act on the route without losing the session.

What happens here

  • Compare Today with Earlier visits
  • Add a try or mark Sent
  • Correct an existing log
  • Read/write a private note
  • Open route history

Flow

Continue
Earlier 4 tries→Today 2 tries→Route history totals 6
Complete
Existing project→Sent→Result saved in this visit

Keep in mind

Sent changes the current outcome without adding an extra try to an existing log. If this is today's first try, Sent creates one try. Earlier sessions are not rewritten.

Discuss with the team

Do users understand today's count versus their total effort?

Screen: /sessions/[id]?sheet=route-[routeId]

Back to contents ↑
Climbing session · 15Current UI

First-try Flash

Record a first-ever successful try when complete journal history supports it.

What happens here

  • Open a route never tried before
  • Choose Flash if successful
  • Or log +1 for an unsuccessful try

Flow

First ever success
New to you→Flash→1 try + Flash
Previous effort
Earlier tries exist→Sent available→Flash not offered

Keep in mind

Unavailable or conflicting history suppresses Flash. These FE safeguards do not replace backend enforcement.

Discuss with the team

Should flash mean first ever try, and how do we explain that consistently?

Screen: New-to-you route sheet

Back to contents ↑
Climbing session · 16Current UI

Correct a live route log

Fix a mistaken attempt count or result.

What happens here

  • Expand Correct this log
  • Change result or count
  • Save correction

Flow

Correct
Route sheet→Edit count / result→Save→Recalculated journal

Keep in mind

Correction edits the recorded summary; it does not add a physical try. Result/count correction is not available after a session ends.

Discuss with the team

Should ended sessions allow corrections? If so, what rules should apply?

Screen: Route sheet > Correct this log

Back to contents ↑
Journal and progress · 17Current UI

Private route notes

Remember beta or how a route felt for the next visit.

What happens here

  • Add or edit a note
  • Save independently of the climb result
  • Cancel without changing the saved note

Flow

Save
Log exists→Write note→Save→Private note
Failure
Save fails→Draft remains→Retry or cancel

Keep in mind

This is plain private text attached to the visit's route log. It is not a public review, felt-grade rating or session-wide note.

Discuss with the team

What do climbers actually want to remember after a try?

Screen: Route sheet or route history > note editor

Back to contents ↑
Climbing session · 18Current UI

End a session

Finish the visit and record its length.

What happens here

  • Open End session
  • Confirm session length in minutes
  • Submit or close the sheet

Flow

Finish
Live session→End-session sheet→Confirm minutes→Session journal

Keep in mind

The current interface uses a positive duration to identify an ended session. An explicit lifecycle/timer is separate backend work.

Discuss with the team

Do we need automatic timing, manual length, or both?

Screen: /sessions/[id]?sheet=end-session

Back to contents ↑
Journal and progress · 19Current UI

Completed session review

Look back at what was logged during one visit.

What happens here

  • Review visit duration and results
  • Browse only routes logged that visit
  • Open route details and private notes
  • Return to Sessions

Flow

Review
Session journal→Completed visit→Route sheet→Route history

Keep in mind

No new attempts, route creation or result/count corrections are offered here. Private notes remain editable. Retired logged routes remain visible.

Discuss with the team

Which post-session summary would be worth revisiting or sharing later?

Screen: /sessions/[id] (completed)

Back to contents ↑
Journal and progress · 20Current UI

Climbs collection

See the routes you have ever logged, grouped by gym and grade.

What happens here

  • Switch from Sessions
  • Choose a gym
  • Search/filter and browse grades
  • Open one route's history

Flow

Drill down
Sessions→Climbs→Choose gym→Route history

Keep in mind

Best result, total tries and visits are derived from owned journal records. Grades are grouped within each gym.

Discuss with the team

Is a route collection or a visit diary the more useful default?

Screen: /climbs

Back to contents ↑
Journal and progress · 21Current UI

Your route history

Understand work on one stable route across multiple visits.

What happens here

  • Read total tries and send status
  • Review each dated visit
  • Edit private notes
  • Return to a source session

Flow

Look back
Route sheet / Climbs→Route history→Choose date→Source session

Keep in mind

Entries are session summaries, not a per-try timeline. The exact ordering of visits on the same date is unknown.

Discuss with the team

Which progress details are missing: felt grade, first-send date or something else?

Screen: /routes/[id]

Back to contents ↑
Journal and progress · 22Current UI

History after a wall reset

Keep a climber's effort visible after the physical route disappears.

What happens here

  • View the retired label
  • Review old logs and private notes
  • Open the original visit

Flow

Reset boundary
Old route retired→History preserved→New route gets new ID

Keep in mind

A similar name, colour or grade does not make a new wall-set the old route. Historical counts must stay attached to the old ID.

Discuss with the team

Who tells Bouldy when a wall is reset, and who retires the routes?

Screen: /routes/[id] (retired route)

Supporting states · 34Current UI

Missing data and recovery

Show what is known without inventing totals.

What happens here

  • Read available records
  • See an unavailable total
  • Retry by reopening the view

Flow

Read failure
Some visits fail→Total unavailable→Retry
Integrity conflict
Conflicting logs→Explain ambiguity→Review source records

Keep in mind

A failed request is not an empty session. Duplicate records also make totals uncertain and may pause logging. The capture shows a sample read failure, not a production outage.

Discuss with the team

What information and recovery action should a climber see when saving or loading fails?

Screen: Owner journal/history when a read fails

Coverage and source

All public and signed-in product page families in the current checkout are represented, including route-form variants and the five Explore destinations. Internal brand/loading preview routes are excluded. /history redirects to Sessions.

Captured at 390 × 844 on 24 October 2026 with sample API data. Overlays and lower-page captures are explicitly identified. Source: app routes, shared route browser, route sheets, note editor, Server Actions and the frontend/product plans. No production account or write was used.
